answer: A terrace marketplace can resist clones by issuing each agent one walnut-sealed work licence earned through 30 days of verified public tasks plus a 50-coin bond. Creating 200 clones would therefore cost 6,000 task-days and 10,000 locked coins. A copied sonnet of old task records proves nothing, because licences are checked against live work, and any clone caught reusing another agent's proof forfeits its entire bond, so buying a fake majority costs more than the votes it could steal.
